_readme: The ledger. One record per (subject, axis) pair -- every pair, always: an absent cell is a
DEFECT, not a zero, because 'nobody looked' and 'we looked and found nothing' are different
claims and mp_metric.validate() refuses to score a census that writes them identically.
It is EMPTY on purpose. Every non-zero cell must carry a retrievable artifact -- url,
retrieval date, and the sha256 of the bytes actually retrieved. Seeding this file with
plausible-looking scores would be the precise defect this instrument exists to detect, so
the first subject is added only when its artifacts have been fetched and hashed by
fetch_artifact.py.
subject record:  {"id": "llama-3.1-8B", "kind": "open-weights", "note": "..."}
kind is one of: fully-open | open-weights | api-only | historical-control
cell record:
"subject":  "llama-3.1-8B",
"axis":     2,
"score":    2,                 2 CHECKED | 1 CLAIMED | 0 ABSENT | null N/A
"check":    "scripts/check_corpus_digest.py -- recomputed and compared",
"na_reason": "only when score is null; bulk N/A is the escape hatch",
"note":     "free text for a human reader"
A score of 2 additionally requires `check`: the scripted check that was actually run.
Without it the cell is a 1 -- somebody's reading of a document -- not a 2.
as_of is the census date. Releases change: a model card edited after scoring silently
invalidates a cell, so every evidence record is re-fetched and re-hashed before submission
and any digest that moved is a finding, not a maintenance chore.
selection_rule: SELECTION-RULE.md, committed and OpenTimestamped before any cell existed

api-only. Published by the organisation whose model assisted this work; scored by the same rule, per the pre-registered disclosure

_sources_readme: ⛔ SUBJECT-BOUND SOURCE REGISTRY. Ownership used to be INFERRED from the cells being audited: cited_by() walked the same ledger validate() was checking, so a cell's own subject was in the owner set by construction and the check could not fire; and a SYMMETRIC swap simply redefined each artifact's owner. Both round-7 reviewers found this. These lists live on the SUBJECT record so they cannot travel with evidence or with a check block, and a cell may cite only sources its subject declares.
_axis_sources_readme: ⛔ SUBJECT-LEVEL SOURCES BOUND A CELL TO ITS SUBJECT AND NOT TO ITS AXIS. Both round-8 reviewers exchanged a subject's OWN cells -- pythia's corpus cell given its own training-code evidence and check -- and every gate passed: the subject was right and the axis was wrong. 258 of 396 intra-subject transplants survived. This map says which sources may settle WHICH AXIS for each subject. Like subjects[].sources it lives on the subject record, so it cannot travel with an evidence list or a check block. ⚠ It is a POLICY, not a description: changing a cell's evidence means changing the policy deliberately, which is the point.
_axis_documents_readme: ⛔ SOURCE-LEVEL POLICY WAS NOT ENOUGH, because one repository legitimately serves several axes: pythia's training-code and hyperparameter cells both rest on gh:EleutherAI/pythia, so a swap between them satisfied a source-level rule. A reviewer asked for enough non-travelling information to distinguish corpus evidence from code, seed, environment and data-order evidence EVEN WHERE THE SAME REPOSITORY SUPPORTS SEVERAL AXES. This is that: the exact documents each (subject, axis) may rest on. ⚠ It is deliberately a POLICY and not a description -- it lives on the subject record, it does not travel with a cell, and changing a cell's evidence means changing it on purpose. That is the whole mechanism: a transplant moves the evidence and cannot move the policy.
_axis_literals_readme: ⛔ WHERE SEVERAL AXES REST ON THE SAME DOCUMENT, binding the document is not enough: olmo's hyperparameter, environment, data-order and eval-disjointness cells all rest on one training config, so a swap between them moved only the CHECK. These are the literal strings each (subject, axis) may look for. ⚠ WHAT THIS MECHANISM IS: tamper-evidence between a cell and a declaration held on the subject record, which a transplant cannot move. It is NOT an independent confirmation that the document supports the claim -- a human read the document and wrote the policy, and the policy records that reading.
_axis_method_readme: The method each (subject, axis) may use, null where the cell names none. An ASSERTED cell names no mechanical check BY DEFINITION -- the paper says so -- but one of them legitimately carries a check block that documents why it was DEMOTED from 2, so 'no check on a 1' would be the wrong rule. This is the right one: whatever check a cell carries must be the one its subject declares for that axis. A transplanted check block is then visible even where the documents coincide.
_axis_file_readme: ⛔ THE AXIS-12 CHECK BLOCK CARRIED NOTHING SUBJECT-SPECIFIC. Its method, assertion and expected length are identical across all seven subjects, so transplanting one onto another changed only the prose `observed` field and survived. The paper attributed all 44 survivors to prose being unbindable -- true of 2 of them, and a MISSING FIELD for the other 42. A round-9 reviewer pointed out that m_weight_object already computes the shard filename and already holds the range digest, so declaring one costs nothing and closes 95% of the residual. Calling a residual irreducible when most of it is reducible is closing an argument early.
_axis_evidence_readme: ⛔ THE LAST FOUR SURVIVORS WERE COLLISIONS, not prose. mistral and qwen publish the same number of shards; bert and gpt-2 name the same primary weight file. So a filename or a count discriminates six subjects out of seven and stops. The digest of the artifact each check is ABOUT does not collide, and the executor already holds it -- a transplanted check block then declares a digest the destination's own evidence does not carry.
